findings.title: Cache key uses Python's per-process randomized hash() of a tuple
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash` is not stable across processes for tuples of ints in all cases, and it can collide. That makes it unsafe for a shared cache (memcached/redis). Colliding project sets would share an eligibility result, so a non-allowlisted set could be told it is eligible, or the reverse. Use a stable key such as a joined sorted id list or a real digest.

findings.title: Allowlist eligibility cached for 60s with no invalidation hook
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere. After the option changes, stale results are served for up to a minute. The cache is also pointless, since `options.get` is already cached in-process. It adds a cache round-trip and staleness for no gain. The docstring's claim that the lookups are expensive is wrong.

findings.title: Allowlist membership test depends on the option's element types
findings.body: `project_id in allowlist` does a linear scan of the option list for every project. If the option contains strings, or ids of a different type, the check silently fails. Convert the allowlist to a set of ints once, then check membership against that set.

findings.title: Discover eligibility is decided by a substring match on the raw request query
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a substring match for `event.type:error` on `request.GET['query']`. This misfires on negated queries (`!event.type:error`), on `event.type:error_foo`, and on any query containing that text in a value. The endpoint also rewrites the query internally, for example adding `AND !event.type:transaction` for the dashboard split. In that case the helper reads the original request query rather than the query actually executed. The result is upsampled counts applied to the wrong queries, or missed for the right ones. Parse the query that is actually run instead.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the closure `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument. The dashboard-split paths call `_get_event_stats` with `discover` or the scoped dataset, and the eligibility decision ignores that. A transaction query or a split-to-transactions query can therefore be rewritten with `upsampled_count`, which reads `sample_weight`, a column transactions do not have. The query can then fail or return wrong data.

findings.title: Transformed `upsampled_count()` is sent to datasets that don't define it
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` emits `upsampled_count() as count`. The function is only registered in the discover dataset's `function_converter`. The errors dataset, and the RPC path at line 277, are not given it. Eligibility returns True for `dataset == errors`, so top-events and RPC queries on those datasets may fail with an unknown-function error. Only count() is rewritten, and the alias is hard-coded to 'count', which would break aliasing for top events that use a different yAxis.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace and misleading comments
findings.body: Lines 223, 234 and 278 (and the cache helper file) have trailing whitespace, which will fail lint. The comments claim 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' and 'late transformation ensures we use most current schema assumptions'. The code does neither, and the check re-runs on every `_get_event_stats` call.

findings.title: upsampled_count() sums sample_weight with no null/zero fallback and is not private
findings.body: `sum(sample_weight)` is used directly. Events ingested without `sample_weight` contribute NULL or 0 and are dropped from the count. Events from before the feature, or from non-sampled SDKs in allowlisted projects, are therefore undercounted. A fallback such as `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` is needed. The function is also publicly exposed (no `private=True`), so users can call it directly. The 'assumes schema guarantees' comments are not backed by anything.

findings.title: Test factory unconditionally rewrites sample_rate on stored events, with swallowed exceptions
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` is applied to every `store_event` call. It overrides `sample_rate` for all tests that happen to include `contexts.error_sampling`. It also wraps everything in bare `except Exception: pass`, which hides malformed data. The helper lives in shared test infrastructure and changes behavior for unrelated tests, so it should be opt-in or narrower.

findings.title: No unit test for the main entry point or the caching behavior
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and the cache and invalidate logic have no unit tests. Only the private helpers are tested. Nothing exercises cache hits, staleness, or the key function. The test also builds a `SnubaParams` that it never uses.

findings.title: Stray submodule/gitlink file committed
findings.body: A `sentry-repo` entry, a subproject commit pointing at the base commit, is added to the repo. It is unrelated to the feature and looks like an accidental commit. It should be removed.
